provenance: Telephone call, 2026-09-13, Larry's son asking the four cold van questions from the head of the interview guide, exactly as written and with nothing else said or shown first, and typing Larry's answers as he spoke them. This answer is to: "What did Sergeant La Franceaous do — what was his job?" Raw capture: research/interviews/breakfast-questions.md, annotated in place under each question. His son corrected two keying slips in this answer shortly after the call, before the record was committed.
text: He was paratrooper and he was kind of in charge of everything. The officers had liked him the best. If something that needed to be repaired, like a radio, they would get ahold of La Franceaous or Ron Tototz. La Franceaous was probably about 5 foot 7 or so. Not a very big guy.
researchNotes: Asked cold. The question supplied the surname (his son's established phonetic rendering) and the rank "Sergeant", both Larry's own from 2026-08-15, and nothing about a role. This is the first context for the man since he was named: a paratrooper, "kind of in charge of everything", the officers' favourite, one of two men sent for when a radio needed repair (the other Ron Tototz), about 5 ft 7 in, "not a very big guy". Against the printed caption in research/units/18th-aod-stars-and-stripes-1964.md, the rank agrees (but it was in the question), and the role he gives is broader and more senior than the printed one. No contradiction, no confirmation. "Paratrooper" is new and checkable, because jump qualification is on a personnel file. It may be the same thing as "they had their own paratroopers" in the outfit answer, and the family brief's "pathfinders". The radio-repair line is the first job anyone has given Ron Tototz (ledger #15). The text is as his son finished typing it that evening: two slips of the keyboard made during the call ("paratropper", "it hey") were corrected by his son before the record was committed. "ahold" is as typed. HIS SON'S NOTES ON THE CALL, same evening: "paratrooper" was a clear statement, and the first thing Larry said in answer to the question. It is not a guess.
